subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests, and must that cache live only inside one reviewer/run with the full reviewed input as its key?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but caching an exec approval reviewer result changes when a later request bypasses a fresh model review, so cache lifetime and key shape need explicit approval-boundary intent.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, without persisting or converting them to durable/session approval.

options.title: Memoize only low-risk allow-once
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once results and keep ask, error, and timeout decisions uncached for a narrower but less complete cost reduction.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept repeated model cost for now to preserve one-request-one-review semantics until stronger security or billing evidence justifies reuse.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, without persisting or converting them to durable/session approval.
